answer: Each bonded identity escrows collateral; proof that k identities coordinated an equivocation triggers slashing proportional to k², so splitting one attacker across a swarm increases rather than fragments liability through pairwise fault links. Detection further applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier through forfeiture and asymmetric depreciation of remaining stake, making concealed coordination costly. A karst registry links proofs, a lantern audit reveals timing correlations, and tundra recovery rules deter cheap re-entry.
